items.question: What certain liberation from calamities follows from resolving on a hundred-thousand recitations?
premises: A hundred-thousand recitations are resolved upon as the practice.
This resolve is held through meditation expressed as 'one should mutter a hundred-thousand'.
Release from calamities is stated to occur as a certain result.
items.inference: Therefore, meditating on the resolve to perform a hundred-thousand recitations certainly brings release from calamities.
uncertainties: Whether japyāt functions strictly as an optative injunction or as part of the contemplated thought marked by iti is context-dependent.
items.plain_english: Having meditated, 'One should mutter a hundred thousand,' one is certainly released from calamities.
